outputs.answer: Searle's Chinese Room thought experiment is meant to show that manipulating symbols according to rules (syntax) is not the same as understanding meaning (semantics), so a program that behaves intelligently does not thereby have a mind. [GAIF-1.3]

A single McCulloch-Pitts neuron can compute AND and OR because these functions are linearly separable—there exists a set of weights and a threshold that can separate the input patterns producing output 1 from those producing output 0. For AND, weights of 1 and 1 with threshold 2 fire only when both inputs are 1; for OR, weights of 2 and 2 with threshold 2 fire when at least one input is 1. However, XOR is not linearly separable: no single threshold can separate the input pairs (0,1) and (1,0) (which should output 1) from (0,0) and (1,1) (which should output 0) using a linear decision boundary. This limitation was demonstrated in the lecture, showing that XOR requires a two-layer network combining "A and not B" with "not A and B" using inhibitory (negative) weights. [GAIF-2.5]

Nick Bostrom defines superintelligence as any intellect that greatly exceeds human cognitive performance in virtually all domains of interest. The pathways discussed are biological cognition (enhancing human brains), whole brain emulation (copying a brain in a computer), and artificial intelligence. [GAIF-1.6]

The vanishing gradient problem occurs when gradients become very small during backpropagation, causing them to approach zero as they are multiplied across many layers, which hinders training of deep networks. ReLU helps because it does not saturate for positive inputs, allowing gradients to flow without diminishing, thus mitigating the vanishing gradient issue. [GAIF-2.14]

outputs.answer: Prompt caching lowers cost by storing the processed front of a context; a later call with a byte-identical prefix is billed at a fraction of the normal input price and answers faster. Precision measures how many of the flagged cases were correct (TP/(TP+FP)), while recall measures how many of the actual cases were caught (TP/(TP+FN)). Accuracy can be misleading on imbalanced data because a large number of true negatives can inflate the score even if the model misses many positive cases. [PEID-5.6]

The difference is who decides the next step: in a workflow, predefined code paths orchestrate the process, while in an agent, the LLM dynamically directs its own process and tool use at runtime. [PEID-4.1]

Cohen's kappa measures agreement between annotators after subtracting the agreement expected by chance, while raw agreement can be high even when annotators are guessing, especially if one label dominates the dataset. [PEID-5.12]

outputs.answer: For every token it produces, the model re-weights all the tokens it has already seen: in "the ticket the customer opened yesterday is still unresolved", the words "ticket" and "customer" get most of the weight and "the" almost none. This weighting is attention. It is learned, not programmed; word order and position matter; and its cost grows with the square of the context length. [PEID-1.4]
